newsitem.title: USA: Calif. revenues at least $305 mln over forecast.
newsitem.headline: Calif. revenues at least $305 mln over forecast.

text.p: California general fund revenues have topped the governor's budget forecast by at least $305 million in fiscal 1996-97, a state finance official said on Wednesday.

From July 1996 through the end of March 1997, state general fund revenues were $305 million above Gov. Pete Wilson's January budget forecast, according to H.D. Palmer, assistant director of the California Department of Finance.

Palmer told Reuters that revenues exceeded the governor's forecast for the month of April. He said the better-than-expected April collections would "improve the state's revenue picture" beyond $305 million. The April results have yet to be released.
Wilson, a Republican, was scheduled to unveil his budget revisions on May 14. His revised budget plan will take the additional revenues into account, Palmer said.
In January, Wilson forecast general fund revenues for fiscal 1996-97 and 1997-98 at $48.4 billion and $50.7 billion, respectively.
General fund revenues and transfers represent about 78 percent of total state revenues. The remaining 22 percent are special funds, dedicated to specific programs.
The state's three largest revenue sources -- personal income, sales and bank and corporation taxes -- account for about 73 percent of total revenues.
